sentences.text: Plesiosaurus was an extinct genus of large marine sauropterygian reptiles that lived during the Early Jurassic.
This animal is distinguished by its small head, long and thin neck, turtle-like wide body, short tail, and two pairs of large flippers.
It possessed simple, needle-like cone teeth that were slightly curved and circular in cross-section.
Compared to other plesiosaur genera, Plesiosaurus had a notably small head.
In adults, the hindlimbs were long and narrow but much smaller than the forelimbs.
None of the hundreds of Jurassic and Cretaceous plesiosaurs referred to Plesiosaurus were correctly assigned to the genus.
Plesiosaurus was among the first antediluvian reptiles discovered and generated great interest in Victorian England.
The name Plesiosaurus was coined by William Conybeare and Henry De la Beche in 1821 based on scattered finds from the Bristol region, Dorset, and Lyme Regis.
The type species Plesiosaurus dolichodeirus was named and described by Conybeare in 1824 based on Mary Anning's original finds.
Fossils are known from nearly complete skeletons found in the Lias formation of England.
English coasts have exposed canteras from the Lower Jurassic Lias Group that produced many of the most important known plesiosaur specimens.
Plesiosaurus likely fed on belemnites, fish, and other prey.
The U-shaped jaw and sharp teeth of Plesiosaurus functioned like a fish trap.
Its U-shaped jaws and sharp teeth may have acted as a trap for fish.
Plesiosaurus moved by paddling its flippers, as its tail was too short to be useful for propulsion.
Plesiosaurus propelled itself with its flippers because its tail was too short to be a locomotor organ.
Researchers suggest Plesiosaurus may have used its long neck as a rudder while navigating during chases.
Its neck may have been used as a rudder when swimming during a chase.
Plesiosaurus gave birth to live young in the water, similar to most sea snakes.
Based on findings in the Cretaceous plesiosaur Polycotylus, Plesiosaurus surely gave birth to its young in the water like sea snakes.
It is hypothesized that Plesiosaurus young lived in estuaries before moving into the open ocean.
Juveniles may have lived in estuaries before moving to the open ocean.
It is debated whether the long neck of Plesiosaurus hindered acceleration by creating turbulence when bent.
Due to potential acceleration issues, Plesiosaurus may have hunted by lying in wait rather than pursuing prey.
The genus Plesiosaurus was named by Conybeare in 1821.
Plesiosaurus gave its name to the order Plesiosauria, of which it is a primitive but typical member.
Plesiosaurus belongs to the parent group Plesiosauroidea.
Plesiosaurus has historically been treated as a wastebasket taxon containing many species that were later reassigned.
Species like P. brachypterygius, P. guilielmiiperatoris, and P. tournemirensis were moved to new genera Hydrorion, Seeleyosaurus, and Occitanosaurus respectively.
Plesiosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic, specifically from the Hettangian to Toarcian stages.
Plesiosaurus lived from the Rhaetian to the Maastrichtian, between 205.7 and 66 million years ago.
